requirement: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its own anchored definition on the current page. The badge MUST have a separate adjacent link containing an accessible right-arrow icon in an integrated segment matching the badge color linking to its evidence detail page. The badge and arrow MUST remain aligned in one non-wrapping row. Definitions MUST NOT be followed by a separate plaintext evidence link. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
rationale: The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.index.navigation`. I found no gap. - **Badge links to its own anchored definition on the current page.** - `definitions_without_a_marker_get_a_default_index_and_detail_pages` asserts `id="habeas-{kind}-rules.{name}" href="#habeas-{kind}-rules.{name}"` for a requirement, an example and a `.md`-containing name. - `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` asserts the same id/href pair for `requirements.core.ready`. - **Separate adjacent arrow link to the evidence detail page.** - `mdbook_preprocessor_renders_definitions_between_stdin_and_stdout` splits out each `habeas-definition-badge` span. It checks that each row has an `` (badge link plus icon link), and that the detail href is `requirements-index/rules.ready.html`. - `index_owns_details_in_book_order_with_badge_icons` checks the `View evidence` title, the aria-label and the `stroke="#fff"` arrow. - `definition_evidence_link_targets_are_escaped` checks the exact escaped href and aria-label on the icon anchor. - **Icon segment matches the badge color.** `definition_badge_and_evidence_icon_share_colors` compares the shield color with the icon `background-color` for both `req` and `example`. In `fn[replace_definitions]` the color depends only on the definition kind, so these two cases cover every variation. - **One non-wrapping aligned row.** `definition_badge_stylesheet_keeps_the_arrow_in_one_row` asserts the wrapper, link and icon CSS declarations: `inline-flex`, `nowrap`, `flex-shrink: 0`, centered alignment and a fixed height. - **No separate plaintext evidence link.** Several tests assert `!content.contains("See evidence")`. - **Detail page links back to the anchored badge and to the index.** - The default-index test checks every detail page for the `[Requirements index](../requirements-index.html)` link. It checks the `[View definition](...#habeas-req-...)` anchored link for the `cli.mdbook` page and the nested-chapter page. - The evidence-states test checks the explicit-index placement. - The ordering test checks the `../../more.html#habeas-example-...` link. - **Reference badges still link to the definition.** `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition` checks the `impl`, `cite` and `test` reference badges. Each links to `../requirements.html#habeas-req-requirements.ready`. - **`.md` in names.** - `links_preserve_requirement_names_containing_md` asserts `%2Emd` encoding for both the detail href and the definition anchor href. - The default-index test and the ordering test also assert `cli%2Emdbook` in the badge, icon and detail-page links. The tests only partly check that the icon is a right arrow (they look for the white stroke, not the path). The test for `.md` names in reference badges goes through `chapter_href` rather than a rendered reference to such a name. Neither is a named obligation with a plausible violation that the tests would accept.
